business_scope.primary_industry_name: Generative Artificial Intelligence and LLM Inference APIs

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa — International Companies Regime (offshore jurisdiction administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA))
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — English Common Law statutory tradition with Samoan customary law (fa'asamoa / matai) elements; the International Companies regime is governed by the International Companies Act 1987 and is construed under common-law principles
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: PACER Plus — Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations Plus (signed 2017, in force for Samoa)
Samoa-Australia Double Taxation Agreement (1980, as amended)
Samoa-New Zealand Double Taxation Agreement (1980, as amended)
WTO Membership — General Agreement on Trade in Services and trade-related investment instruments

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Anti-Money Laundering and Countering Financing of Terrorism Act 2019, as amended; Financial Intelligence Unit Act 2011; Samoa International Finance Authority Act 2000; AML/CFT Compliance Guidelines issued by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit; Pacific AML/CFT peer-review measures as adopted by Samoa

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Registrar of International Companies
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille — Samoa is a Contracting State to the Hague Apostille Convention; the competent authority for issuing apostilles is the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; consular legalization applies only where the destination state is not a party to the Convention

Hague Apostille issued by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; alternative chain: notarization by a Samoan notary public, authentication by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade, and consular legalization at the destination-country consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Memorandum and Articles of Association (certified copy)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Samoan notary public and Hague Apostille by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; alternative chain: consular legalization for non-Convention destination states

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Registered Agent's Certificate of Beneficial Ownership and Corporate Structure
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a Samoan notary public and Hague Apostille by the Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; alternative chain: consular legalization for non-Convention destination states

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, and authorised signatories against the consolidated watch-list of the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit, the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) and Sectoral Sanctions Identifications list, the UN Security Council Consolidated List (including ISIL and Al-Qaida, Taliban, and other UN sanctions regimes), the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and the domestic Samoan restrictive-measures framework; enhanced due diligence is automatically required for politically exposed persons, correspondent relationships, and any persons residing in or transacting with high-risk or non-cooperative jurisdictions; risk-based ongoing monitoring, source-of-wealth verification, and periodic re-screening at least annually or upon any material change are mandated under the AML/CFT Act 2019 and the Samoa FIU guidelines.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Company Registry — name clearance and reservation are undertaken exclusively through a licensed registered agent using SIFA's approved electronic filing channel (SIFA online registry services) or by written application to the Registrar of International Companies; direct public self-service online reservations are not permitted for International Companies
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Where the proposed name includes any character not in the standard Latin alphabet, the applicant must provide a transliteration in Latin characters and a certified English or Samoan translation; the registered name must be in a language and script acceptable to the Registrar and must not offend public policy or Samoan custom; the name must terminate with an acceptable legal designator such as 'Limited', 'Corporation', 'Incorporated', 'Societe Anonyme', 'Ltd', 'Corp', 'Inc' or an approved abbreviation; the name must not be identical or deceptively similar to any name appearing on the SIFA register or on any other business-name register of the Registrar; a Samoan-language name must include the Latin-alphabet equivalent and is subject to linguistic-accuracy review by the Registrar.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Registrar refuses a proposed name, the licensed registered agent may, within 14 calendar days of the refusal notice, file a written administrative reconsideration request with the Registrar of International Companies, citing the statutory basis for compliance of the name with the International Companies Act 1987 and the SIFA name-clearance guidelines; the Registrar must respond with a reasoned determination within 21 calendar days; an aggrieved applicant may thereafter appeal to the Minister responsible for international financial services, and ultimately apply to the Supreme Court of Samoa for judicial review under the Judicature Ordinance 1961 and applicable constitutional review principles; no fee is refunded upon rejection, and a fresh name reservation with an updated proposed name is treated as a new application.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A physical registered office is statutorily mandatory and must be maintained at the address of a licensed registered agent in Samoa; a post-office box alone or a pure virtual address is not acceptable as the registered office. For the remote AI/LLM API platform, the physical registered office serves as the legal seat for service of process, maintenance of the statutory registers (members, directors, charges, and beneficial ownership records), and the principal records depository. A virtual office or virtual correspondence address may be used solely for auxiliary administrative correspondence, customer-support mail, and payment-rail onboarding (e.g., Stripe, USDC/cryptocurrency exchanges), provided it does not operate as the statutory seat or misrepresent the company's physical location; in practice, the registered agent's physical office in Apia will be registered and displayed as the official registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 10-15% per annum for a low-risk ISIC 6201 generative AI and LLM API token provider that maintains up-to-date registers, a compliant licensed registered agent, and no adverse intelligence; the risk rises to above 50% per annum if AML/CFT filings are deficient, the UBO register is incomplete or untimely, sanctions screening reveals unresolved matches, or any tax or regulatory red flags are raised; SIFA and the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit are authorised to carry out unannounced physical inspections, spot audits, and on-demand production of corporate books under the International Companies Act 1987 and the AML/CFT Act 2019.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation fee — International Company
Certificate of Incorporation and initial company registration fee (no minimum capital requirement)
Certificate of Good Standing / certified extract (first issuance for the incorporation bundle)
Licensed registered agent annual professional fee, including registered office, statutory records custody, and company secretarial services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — flat annual corporate maintenance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT client onboarding, UBO identification and verification, PEP/sanctions screening, and risk rating (one-time compliance package)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / compliance officer (private sector)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — fixed onboarding compliance fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, Hague Apostille / consular legalization and courier for the corporate document bundle (Certificate of Incorporation, Memorandum and Articles of Association, UBO certificate) for use with banks, Stripe, and cryptocurrency exchanges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Samoan notary public; Samoan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade; destination-country consular authority; international courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff, Government apostille fee schedule, consular legalization fee schedule, and prevailing market courier/legalization service fee

Supplementary virtual correspondence address (optional) for remote AI API platform administrative mail handling
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed registered agent / virtual office service provider (private sector)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark — annual subscription fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2015, read as a whole — incorporating the statutory provisions on application for incorporation, name restrictions, memorandum and articles, share capital, registered office, directors and secretary; supplemented by the International Companies (Fees) Regulations 2004 and the International Companies (Registered Agents) Regulations 1992.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa — applications are lodged exclusively through a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent under the supervision of the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form 1 — Application for Incorporation of an International Company, accompanied by the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association and the registered agent's consent notice.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow or bank-deposit requirement. The subscriber may issue one fully paid Ordinary Share of no par value with stated consideration of US$1.00; authorized share capital is set in the Memorandum (commonly US$1,000,000) and paid-up amount is left to subscriber discretion.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding shareholder's subscription is ratified and one fully paid Ordinary Share of no par value is allotted in the electronic share register. RESOLVED, that the registered office at the licensed agent's premises in Apia, Samoa is adopted as the statutory registered office, and the agent is instructed to file all required notices. RESOLVED, that [Director Name] is appointed sole Director and [Secretary Name] is appointed Company Secretary, each to serve under the Articles. RESOLVED, that the Director is authorized to open accounts and execute payment-facilitator agreements (Stripe, USDC) and to effect all statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (via a SIFA-licensed Registered Agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit a name-approval application listing at least two distinct corporate names, each containing a required suffix such as 'International Company' or 'IC'. The Registered Agent lodges the application under the name-restriction provisions of the ICA, verifies absence of conflict with the live registry pool, and also validates availability of the Chinese-language parallel name for the target clientele. Upon written clearance, the name is reserved for 30 days pending incorporation.
required_dossiers: Name approval application (Registrar's prescribed form)
Letter of engagement to the SIFA-licensed Registered Agent
Passport copy and residential address of proposed shareholder and director
Agent's confirmation of the proposed Chinese-language company name (if parallel name adopted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name is refused for similarity, obscenity, or because it is reserved, the agent immediately files the second-choice name; the Registrar's refusal is not appealable in practice, but a revised application attracting no additional government fee can be resubmitted within the 30-day reservation window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting, Execution and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed Registered Agent (acting as notary public) and founding subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent drafts the Memorandum and Articles in English (the statutory language, with an optional Chinese-language translation appended for the beneficial owner), sets the authorized share capital and no-par-value share class, and arranges signature by the subscriber. Each subscriber signature is witnessed and notarially certified by the agent, who retains the original signed documents at its Samoan office in compliance with the ICA and AML/CFT (SAMOA) Act obligations.
required_dossiers: Subscriber passport copies and proof of address
Professional or banker's reference letter (KYC file)
Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association for subscriber review
Optional Chinese-language translation of Memorandum and Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar or the agent identifies a defect (e.g., inconsistent share class or incorrect subscriber identity), the document is promptly revised and re-executed with a substituted signature page; re-notarization is performed by the same licensed agent at no additional statutory fee, and any affected page is re-filed with the application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Lodgment of Form 1 Application and Payment of Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Office of the Registrar of International Companies, MCIL (Apia); payment processed via the integrated SIFA registry e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Registered Agent files Form 1 together with the notarized Memorandum and Articles and the agent's consent; simultaneously pays the government incorporation fee (approximately US$600 inclusive of certificate fee). The registry issues a stamped acknowledgment with an application number; any outstanding AML declarations or director consents are submitted within the same lodgment package.
required_dossiers: Form 1 — Application for Incorporation of an International Company
Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (original)
Consent of Registered Agent to act
Statutory declaration or consent of the proposed director if required by registry policy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Upon a deficiency notice from the Registrar, the agent files the corrected schedule within 14 days of the notice; where correction is impossible, Form 1 is withdrawn and refiled, and the already-paid fee is credited toward the new application as a matter of registry administrative practice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Allotment of Initial Share
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies (certificate); Registered Agent's office (share ledger)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following successful examination, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company number and date of incorporation. Concurrently, the subscriber executes an allotment instrument subscribed for one Ordinary Share of no par value with stated consideration US$1.00; the share is entered in the electronic share register at the registered office, and the sole director signs the share certificate.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Registrar
Allotment instrument or subscriber resolution
Electronic share register (maintained by the agent)
Share certificate for the allotted Ordinary Share
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains a clerical error (incorrect number or date), the agent files a written Request for Administrative Correction and obtains a reissued certificate within 3 business days; if issuance is delayed, the agent expedites through the Registrar's client-service desk using the application number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of First Board Resolution — Officers and Registered Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors; the Registered Agent as statutory registered-office keeper (no public officer filing is required under the ICA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole director passes the formal First Board Resolution (see pro-forma text in the Legal Framework block) by written consent, ratifying the allotment, adopting the Apia registered office, and appointing the sole director and company secretary. Executed minutes and signed consents to act are deposited at the registered office, and the register of directors and officers is updated; no filing with the Registrar is required for officer appointments unless the registered office or agent changes.
required_dossiers: Signed First Board Resolution minutes
Consent to act signed by the director and the secretary
Updated Register of Directors and Officers
Registered-office confirmation letter issued by the agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the appointed officer declines consent or the agent objects, the board passes a supplementary resolution naming a substitute officer; where the registered agent relationship terminates, a Notice of Change of Registered Agent is filed with the Registrar within 28 days and the resolution is re-deposited with the successor agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Operational Onboarding — Tax-Exemption Confirmation, Banking and Digital Payment Rails
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA); commercial banks and fintech payment processors (Stripe, USDC custody platforms)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The agent obtains from SIFA a confirmation of the International Company's automatic income-tax exemption, which is furnished to banks and counterparties. The company completes account opening (where physical banking is required) and merchant KYC for Stripe and USDC payment rails, submitting the incorporation pack. The Beneficial Ownership Register extract is filed with the agent in line with Samoan anti-money-laundering requirements, and the billing jurisdiction profile (Samoa IC, no Samoan VAT) is documented for the API pricing page.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Incumbency
Memorandum and Articles of Association
Register of Directors, Officers and Shareholders
Beneficial Ownership Register extract
Bank and professional references for Stripe/USDC provider due diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a payment processor requests enhanced due diligence, the agent issues a legal-opinion letter and director certificate within 1 business day; if SIFA's exemption letter is questioned, the company supplies its cloud-service contracts and audited confirmation of no Samoan-source income, and the agent re-issues the SIFA certificate under the relevant certificate-on-demand procedure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — exempt. A Samoa International Company engaged in ISIC 6201 generative-AI/LLM API services is an offshore digital service with no manufacturing plant or physical facility, and therefore falls outside the MCIL industrial/Business Licensing framework.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — Samoa imposes no dedicated 'cloud-service provider', 'data-center' or 'AI-platform' operating permit; as an International Company, the entity is deemed to carry on business wholly outside Samoa and is exempt from domestic occupation-licensing requirements.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA) — Samoa's EIA authority under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no construction, land disturbance, stationary emissions or physical discharge in Samoa. The AI/LLM service is delivered through overseas cloud infrastructure, so no EIA preliminary assessment report, environmental permit, or waste registration is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable while no Samoan premises or servers exist. Should a local office or colocation node be established later, the World Bank Group/IFC General EHS Guidelines will govern: wastewater BOD ≤ 25 mg/L and TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, electronics-waste segregation and disposal under the Samoa Waste Management Act 2005, and applicable ITU telecom-equipment emission limits for any deployed hardware.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not applicable — there is no physical workplace in Samoa to certify. The online-only configuration imposes no civil-defense obligations. If a future Apia office is opened, the following become mandatory before occupancy: fire-safety certificate under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2006, structural-load and building-permit clearance under the Samoa Building Code 2012, and occupational-safety certification under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1986 (as amended 2018).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Apia, Samoa — statutory tax administration under the Tax Administration Act 2012; official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws (MfR e-Services). The International Companies Act 1987 is administered by the International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), which issues the IC Certificate of Incorporation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A licensed Samoa registered agent incorporates the International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 and obtains the Certificate of Incorporation from the MCIL International Companies Registry. Step 2: The agent submits a TIN application (MfR TIN form) via MfR e-Services, attaching the Certificate of Incorporation, the agent's licence, and director/shareholder identification. Step 3: MfR issues the Samoa Tax Identification Number (TIN) within 3–5 business days; because the IC is statutorily tax-exempt, no income tax or VAGST registration is required or effected. Step 4: For bank account opening and corporate counterparty verification, the IC furnishes the TIN, Certificate of Incorporation, and a registered-agent certificate confirming its exempt offshore status.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch election exists under Samoan law. The IC is statutorily fixed as a separate legal person and fully tax-exempt offshore entity under the International Companies Act 1987; its classification cannot be elected, varied, or waived domestically. Foreign classification elections (e.g., U.S. Form 8832) operate only under overseas tax law and do not alter Samoan treatment.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Goods and Services Tax ('VAGST') — Samoa's VAT-type indirect tax under the VAGST Act 2012
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 120,000 (Samoa Tala) of taxable supplies in any 12 consecutive months (VAGST Act 2012, s. 11). The exempt IC is outside the scope of VAGST registration at any turnover level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: None. Samoa imposes no real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or API-based e-invoicing obligation. VAGST-registered suppliers must issue tax invoices containing the particulars prescribed by the VAGST Act 2012 (s. 87) and file monthly returns through MfR e-Services; the IC has no invoicing or filing obligations for offshore AI-API revenue.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAGST Act 2012, exported services supplied to a non-resident who is outside Samoa at the time of supply — including SaaS and LLM/AI API token-metered services — qualify for 0% zero-rating. However, the Samoa IC is statutorily exempt from VAGST on all offshore income; consequently, its subscription and usage-token revenue (whether settled in USD or USDC) is subject to a 0% effective rate with no requirement to register, charge, file, or recover VAGST.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — inapplicable to intangible AI-API services; operative export evidence is the executed SaaS/API licence agreement between the IC and the non-resident customer
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill — not issued for digital services; replaced by the IC's token-usage report or metered-billing ledger documenting services rendered to offshore counterparties

Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/Stripe settlement statement — issued by a Samoa licensed commercial bank or payment processor, evidencing receipt of foreign currency (USD/USDC) from non-resident clients
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: MfR may re-open assessments and recover unwarranted refunds or tax within the statutory amendment period (generally 5 years; extended in cases of fraud). Export zero-rating or exemption obtained through false declarations is penalized under the Tax Administration Act 2012 by culpability-tiered shortfall penalties (up to 150% of the tax shortfall), statutory interest, criminal fines, and imprisonment for responsible officers. An IC that trades with Samoan residents or otherwise breaches the non-resident conditions of the International Companies Act 1987 forfeits its exemption and becomes retrospectively exposed to VAGST, income tax, and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan tālā (WST) is not fully convertible on a capital-account basis. Current-account payments, including remittances for services and profits, generally may proceed through authorized dealers if supported by evidence of the underlying commercial transaction and tax clearance. Capital-account flows, including inbound equity investment and outbound repatriation of capital, are subject to CBS exchange-control approval under the Exchange Control Act 1971 and the Financial Institutions Regulations. Profit remittance requires documented distributable profits, audited financial statements and proof of settlement of all Samoan tax liabilities. Non-resident International Companies carrying on exclusively offshore business enjoy exchange-control exemptions that extend to their offshore accounts, but any on-island local expenditure must be made through licensed dealers. Cryptocurrency-based remittances are prohibited for WST conversion unless the receipt has been validated through a CBS-regulated fiat on-ramp and the purpose code and source-of-funds documentation are preserved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBS exchange-control practice, export proceeds from Samoan-origin goods must be repatriated to Samoa within 90 days of the date of shipment and must be credited to an exchange-control approved foreign-currency account held with a licensed commercial bank. Goods exports are subject to a mandatory surrender ratio of 100% of proceeds into WST unless an exemption has been granted for debt service, insured reinvoicing or capital goods replacement. Services and digital exports, including AI/LLM API token sales, are not subject to hard surrender percentages; however, all proceeds must be repatriated and accounted for within 180 days. Exporters must register with CBS and file exchange-control forms documenting invoice value, collection details, and any balances retained offshore. Failure to surrender within the statutory timeline may result in a 20% penalty assessment and suspension of FX purchase facilities.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Samoa does not issue electronic money institution (EMI) licences to non-bank fintech entities. Foreign digital EMIs such as Wise, Airwallex or Stripe Treasury may be used solely as payment aggregation rails, but their balances cannot be treated as Samoa-regulated deposits and they are not permitted to open CBS credit-clearing accounts. A licensed Samoa commercial bank is required as the principal clearing counterparty and the ultimate custody bank for all WST-denominated and foreign-currency corporate funds. The use of an offshore EMI as the sole treasury rail is not viable because of legal uncertainty regarding sanctity of funds, FIN-NET remittance compliance and CBS anti-money-laundering oversight.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For an International Company banking in Samoa, the CBS-compliant onboarding process typically requires at least one executive director or a designated senior officer to attend a physical interview at the bank’s head office or a recognized APAC/U.S. correspondent office. Full remote opening is generally not permitted for International Companies that conduct a material cross-border digital business and hold funds in WST. Banks may allow the remaining directors to complete remote verification if accompanied by notarized passports, corporate records, a board resolution, and a professional intermediary undertaking. A purely virtual onboarding with no physical meeting will be treated as a high-risk exception and requires escalation to CBS before an account is opened.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border digital-service revenue with no established physical business premises in Samoa
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master software license agreements, redacted API customer log, technical architecture description showing no unlicensed financial services, audited revenue trail mapping token purchases to genuine AI service consumption, and a written opinion confirming that the business scope does not fall within banking, money service business, or stored-value activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cryptocurrency USDC as a target payment rail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Regulated exchange transaction lists, on-chain wallet address attestation, chainalysis or similar screening reports, a legal memorandum demonstrating USDC is not a derivative of WST or a forbidden crypto-to-fiat casino system, and a written treasury policy that all USDC received is immediately converted to WST/USD through a licensed virtual asset service provider prior to operational use.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity arising from the International Company law and nominee shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Central Beneficial Ownership Register, signed declaration of ultimate beneficial owner, certificate of incorporation, register of directors and subscribers, notarized nominee declaration with irrevocable proxy, and independent third-party identity verification of all natural-person beneficiaries.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of the tax-exempt International Company status for alleged tax evasion
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CBS and Ministry for Revenue tax-exemption certificate, current tax standing letter, proof that the IC is not engaged in domestic trade or physical Samoan-source activity, substance documentation for management and control, and an opinion addressing OECD and Samoa Economic Substance requirements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity token revenue inconsistent with traditional invoice clawback patterns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed KYC-on-tooling protocols, IP-address compliance reporting, sandbox consumption billing, over-refund prevention audit, and a statutory declaration affirming that no funds circulate from sanctioned jurisdictions or organized crime networks.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound shareholder capital and seed funding must be directed through the Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Ltd or Samoa Commercial Bank Ltd using a pre-advised SWIFT MT103 wire. The remittance instruction must clearly cite the entity's International Company number and the phrase 'Subscription for Ordinary Shares — WS_IC'. CBS does not mandate a specific purpose code, but banks require a standard economic purpose such as 'Capital injection for technology operations'; the bearer must submit a board resolution, share subscription agreement, source-of-funds affidavit, passport copies of subscribing shareholders, and a beneficial ownership declaration. For regulated jurisdictions, the sending bank must be pre-approved under the receiving bank's clearing limits. Crypto-backed inbound injections are not accepted at the banking layer and must be converted through a CBS-compliant FSP before settlement.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound operating disbursements must be routed via SWIFT MT103 for amounts below USD 100,000 and SWIFT MT103 plus MT202 cover for larger transfers. Recurring supplier and trade settlements may use Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit opened by the Samoa clearing bank under UCP600, with the IC named as applicant and the overseas service provider as beneficiary. For low-value token disbursements to software vendors, SWIFT MT103 with reference to the invoiced contract and proof of digital-service consumption is permitted. Where a Samoa bank cannot directly connect to the beneficiary jurisdiction, the transfer is cleared via the bank's international correspondent network, typically through Australia, Hong Kong, or Singapore; the IC must maintain a full invoice, contract and delivery-document file because these papers accompany the FX control declaration for each transfer.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable WST/USD forward contracts with a CBS-licensed commercial bank exempt from prior approval if the contract is trade-related

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) transacted with offshore counterparties only where the offshore NDF is back-to-back with an onshore on-balance sheet transaction and approved by CBS as risk-neutralizing
Cross-currency swaps (WST/USD, WST/non-major currencies) under a unilateral treasury policy approved by CBS in advance, provided the IC demonstrates genuine commercial exposure
Over-the-counter FX options where the premium is paid in freely usable foreign currency and CBS approval is received prior to maturity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Licence Fee - annual renewal of the International Company's registration and tax-exempt status
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority / Registrar of International Companies (payment effected by the licensed Samoan registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable annually on the anniversary of incorporation; a 30-day administrative grace period is commonly observed before penalty assessment. The official tariff is denominated in Samoan Tala (WST); the USD figure reflects the standard authorized-capital tier at prevailing exchange rates.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late penalty of 10% of the annual fee applies for each month or part-month that the fee remains unpaid; non-payment beyond approximately three months exposes the company to involuntary administrative strike-off, forfeiture of assets to the Samoan Government, and loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return - annual particulars statement covering registered office, registered agent, directors, shareholders, and share capital
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (filed through the licensed Samoan registered agent)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No standalone government fee, but the Annual Return is not accepted while the annual licence fee is outstanding. Late filing exposes the company to the Registrar's penalty powers and, if unresolved after statutory notice, strike-off under sections 105-106 of the International Companies Act 1987.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: International Companies Beneficial Ownership Return - annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation reflecting all share transfers executed during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (filed by the registered agent maintaining the Register of Beneficial Owners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrent with the Annual Return, within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Materially false, incomplete, or omitted UBO information is a statutory offence carrying monetary fines and disqualification of directors; overdue confirmation suspends renewal eligibility and may trigger default strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Notification and substance self-assessment (applicability to be re-assessed each year; relevant where the LLM/AI API platform exploits intellectual property or supplies in-scope services from Samoa)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority / Registrar of International Companies (economic substance filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Concurrent with the annual renewal cycle; notification due within 30 calendar days after the anniversary of incorporation for any year in which a relevant activity is conducted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, or filing demonstrating inadequate economic substance, attracts statutory monetary penalties, potential exchange of information with foreign tax authorities, refusal of renewal, and ultimately administrative strike-off.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None applicable. Samoa International Companies are exempt from compulsory statutory audit under the International Companies Act 1987 irrespective of turnover, total assets, or shareholder count. An audit is triggered only by the company's articles or shareholder resolution, a regulated-sector licence (banking/insurance), or a specific direction of the Registrar - none of which applies to this AI/LLM API platform.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No statutory accounting basis is prescribed for International Companies; IFRS (including IFRS for SMEs) is the prevailing market standard. The International Company must retain accounting records that fairly reflect transactions and permit preparation of financial statements, but no financial statements are filed or made publicly available with the Samoan Registrar.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: At each renewal cycle the licensed registered agent issues a UBO confirmation declaration; directors and each known beneficial owner must re-declare the ultimate ownership chain and identify any change from the prior year. Share transfers executed during the year must be recorded contemporaneously in the Register of Members and the Register of Beneficial Owners, and the annual confirmation must disclose the pre- and post-transfer positions. The registered agent files the signed confirmation with the Registrar; failure to produce it within the renewal window grounds the renewal and exposes both the company and the agent to regulatory penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (shareholders' and directors' meeting minutes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 450 - USD 1,100 per year (licensed Samoan registered agent and registered office, excluding government fees and disbursements)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 - statutory audit not required; voluntary certified audit or agreed-upon-procedures report sought by payment processors or investors: USD 4,000 - USD 9,000 per engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% for an International Company (IC) under s.86 International Companies Act 1987, which grants total exemption from Samoan income tax; the domestic Samoan corporate headline rate is 27% but is inapplicable to an IC.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Total statutory tax exemption: no income tax, no capital gains tax, no stamp duty, and no withholding tax on IC income or distributions. The IC's annual fiscal burden is limited to a flat annual government fee (USD 300 to USD 5,000 by authorized capital band), plus registered agent and SIFSA service fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: SIFSA Annual Renewal and Exempt-Status Declaration (International Companies Act 1987, s.187); lodgment is effected by a licensed registered agent through the SIFSA e-Services filing portal. No Samoan corporate income tax return is required for an exempt IC.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing and payment due within 60 days after each anniversary of the certificate of incorporation; a late-payment surcharge accrues from the 61st day.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered IC name, unique IC registration number, and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the exact name per certificate of incorporation; a separate trading name may be used only if formally reserved and disclosed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Samoan registered office street address and details of the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors and shareholders must maintain the registered office through the agent; a PO Box is not accepted in the physical address field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital and issued classes/shares outstanding.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No minimum capital applies; any percentage of non-resident ownership must be accurately declared because the tax exemption is voided if the IC conducts business with Samoan residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the registers of directors, shareholders, and charges are physically maintained at the registered office.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The agent may custody the registers; ultimate beneficial owners must satisfy KYC and AML/CFT Act 2018 due diligence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of continued s.86 exemption: no Samoan-source income, no domestic business activity, and no Samoan resident clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Select 'No Samoan-source activity' only if factually true; use of a Samoan bank account or onboarding of Samoan customers constitutes domestic activity and destroys the exemption.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: ESR declaration identifying relevant activity, location of core income generating activities, and presence of directors and staff in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a generative AI / LLM API platform, classify the relevant activity as IP business (high-risk) and evidence local staff, premises, and expenditure; a pure equity-holding IC with no operating subsidiaries may declare low-risk only if factually accurate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Government fee calculated on authorized capital bands plus the SIFSA filing fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Settlement is by corporate card or wire transfer; cryptocurrency is not accepted for Samoan statutory fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Automatic 10% surcharge on the annual fee once payment is overdue; continued default leads to deregistration/striking-off, vesting of assets in the Registrar, a restoration fee plus all arrears, and personal liability of directors for obligations incurred after default.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Samoa imposes no dividend withholding tax on distributions made by an International Company; dividends may be paid freely without Samoan tax or exchange control approval.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: An IC is exempt from Samoan tax and therefore is not a Samoan tax resident for DTA purposes; the Samoan Ministry for Revenue will not issue a Tax Residence Certificate for an exempt IC. Distributions from the IC to non-resident shareholders attract 0% Samoan withholding tax and require no Samoan DTA filing. Any concession in the shareholder's residence country must be substantiated with the shareholder's own TRC; Samoan DTAs (Australia and New Zealand) do not provide benefits to exempt ICs because the IC is not liable to Samoan tax. The IC should maintain audited profit and dividend documentation for foreign tax audits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Samoan statutory withholding rate is 0% on royalty and interest payments made by an IC to non-residents. Under the Samoa-Australia and Samoa-New Zealand treaties, conventional source-country caps are generally 15% on dividends, 10% on interest, and 10% on royalties; however, an exempt IC holds no treaty residence entitlement, so any source-country withholding in customer markets applies at domestic statutory rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: N/A (0 WST) for International Companies: the s.86 exemption removes all income tax and transfer pricing filing obligations. If accidental domestic tax-resident activity arises, Samoa's Income Tax Act 2012 arm's-length rules apply to related-party cross-border transactions without a codified monetary threshold, and Master File / Local File duties attach only where a Samoan domestic resident entity is present in the structure.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa's Economic Substance Regulations (effective 1 January 2022) apply to International Companies. A generative AI / LLM API platform is treated as IP-relevant business; the core income generating activities (strategic technology direction, contract negotiation, AI model deployment control, cost and treasury management) must be performed in Samoa with adequate qualified staff physically present, suitable premises, and local operating expenditure proportionate to revenue. An annual ESR notification is filed via the registered agent with SIFSA. Non-compliance triggers SIFSA administrative penalties, deregistration, and criminal liability for knowingly false ESR declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The AI/LLM API business, token pricing, model inference operations, and customer contracts are all directed and controlled from a foreign jurisdiction while the Samoa IC files a false ESR declaration claiming these CIGAs occur in Samoa.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFSA administrative penalties per breach, deregistration, and revocation of the s.86 tax exemption; a deregistered IC may not invoice customers, and ownership of its receivables, Stripe reserve, and crypto treasury is statutorily defective.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false ESR declarations face criminal prosecution for false statements, fines in penalty units, and imprisonment; courts may disregard the corporate veil and hold directors jointly liable for unpaid creditors and for assisting tax fraud in customer-market jurisdictions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe card revenues and USDC without performing beneficial-owner and transaction monitoring; allowing the API platform to launder stolen tokens by mixing crypto before onward distribution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines and sanctions under Samoa's AML/CFT Act 2018 against the IC and its registered agent for failure to maintain AML programs, keep records, and file suspicious transaction reports; assets involved are subject to confiscation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knew or were wilfully blind to laundering face imprisonment of up to 14 years; travel bans, asset-freezing orders, and civil restitution to victims are also available.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Marketing the tax-exempt IC as a 'zero-tax' shell to conceal beneficial ownership and hide revenue from AI/LLM API sales from the shareholder's residence tax authority.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Samoa imposes no tax on the IC, but the shareholder's home country may recharacterize the IC as a sham, impose civil tax-fraud penalties of 50%-150% of the tax, and obtain financial information under Samoa's TIEAs; foreign courts may enforce restitution against the IC's assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who organized the concealment are exposed to foreign civil restitution judgments, travel restrictions, extradition risk, and imprisonment for tax fraud; the corporate veil is pierced for fraud, and Samoan courts will not enforce the IC's exemption as a shield against foreign criminal process.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to pay the annual government fee or file the SIFSA renewal within the statutory anniversary window.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: 10% surcharge on arrears, deregistration, loss of legal capacity to contract, and vesting of the IC's bank balances, Stripe reserve, and crypto holdings in the Registrar.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for the IC's obligations incurred after the default date; striking off does not discharge directors; restoration requires payment of all arrears, penalties, and court costs, and a deregistered IC cannot sue to collect unpaid AI platform receivables.
